newsitem.title: PERU: Peru seeks $1 billion to halve drug-growing areas.
newsitem.headline: Peru seeks $1 billion to halve drug-growing areas.

text.p: Peru wants rich nations to help finance a five-year, $1 billion project to halve the amount of land used to grow coca leaf, the raw product for cocaine, Health Minister Marino Costa Bauer said on Sunday.

The world's largest grower of coca leaf, Peru aims to use its improved relations with the international financial community to secure loans and donations for programs encouraging farmers to substitute coca for coffee, cocoa, corn or cotton, he said.

"The idea is to find within five years $1 billion -- an amount to be raised by the Peruvian government, the United States and European Union countries," Costa told Peru's leading financial daily, Gestion.

After restructuring its debt with the Paris Club of rich creditor nations in 1996, the government asked the group earlier this year for help with the plan to halve the amount of coca fields in Peru to 45,000 hectares, Costa said.

Germany has said it is willing to write-off $120 million in debt to help the project. The Peruvian government also hoped to secure financing from Japan and Canada toward a second $1 billion five-year scheme, currently being designed to start in 2002, he said.

Peru's success in reducing the country's number of drug-running routes has driven the price of coca leaf low enough to give its alternative-crop programs a real chance of working for the first time in decades, according to U.S. embassy officials.
